name: Dressler & Kang Wool Overcoat
description:
A single-breasted overcoat in a dense charcoal melton wool, cut with the kind of long, clean line that makes a person look like they've made a decision. Peak lapels, two welted hip pockets, a single back vent. The lining is a deep burgundy silk-analog printed with a small geometric pattern — almost invisible until the coat swings open. Buttons are matte black horn.

Dressler & Kang occupy the upper edge of Tier 3 pricing — expensive enough to feel like an investment, not so expensive that it screams corporate. Their overcoats are worn by mid-level analysts who want to look serious without looking like a Vantablack ad, by architects and consultants, by the kind of people who own one very good coat instead of several mediocre ones. The silhouette is timeless in the way that only very well-cut things can be.
what_it_says: You understand quality without needing to announce it. You are probably the most competent person in the room.
worn_by: Tier 3 professionals who dress above their tier
story_hooks: A specific run of Dressler & Kang overcoats was commissioned by a law firm for their entire senior staff — six of those lawyers are now dead under unrelated circumstances.
The silk-analog lining pattern, examined closely, contains a repeating motif that an art historian recognizes as a pre-war encoded document format.
Dressler & Kang's tailoring shop on the Tier 3 commercial strip is a known dead-drop location — the owner knows nothing about it.
